text:
Recent research distinguishes complementarity from similarity and co-purchase. ECCR (2024) defines coherent complements through compatibility and relevance: products bought together can still be incompatible. MGFRec (2026) likewise motivates grounding reasoning in actual catalog items to reduce overinterpretation of user interests. For these probes, the practical implication is to require identifiable title/description evidence for device models, interfaces, formats, or prerequisites; shared vocabulary alone cannot establish compatibility. ([ECCR](https://www.amazon.science/publications/explainable-and-coherent-complement-recommendation-based-on-large-language-models), [MGFRec](https://doi.org/10.1145/3770854.3780206))

AbstentionBench (2025) finds uncertainty handling remains unreliable across frontier models; stronger reasoning and explicit abstention prompts do not solve it. A suitable diagnostic design would separate supported compatibility, explicit incompatibility, and insufficient evidence. Report evidence coverage alongside error rates among decided cases. Missing prerequisite evidence should produce “prerequisite unknown,” rather than “user lacks prerequisite.” Likewise, distinguish exact duplicate identifiers, likely alternate editions, and functionally similar substitutes; metadata similarity cannot establish redundancy or continued ownership. These are proposed operational rules, not validated findings for the twenty users. ([AbstentionBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.09038))

Purchase-intent evidence needs similar restraint. A 2026 conversation audit found recommendations frequently observable but subsequent buying decisions largely unrecorded; missing commitment was not evidence of rejection. For the twenty users, calibrate rejection reasons only against explicit feedback, and distinguish “would choose now,” “plausible complement,” “reject,” and “uncertain.” Report counts and disagreements by category; do not infer diversity/conformity traits, ownership, or immediate intent from histories alone. ([Purchase Advice and Observable Buyer Responses](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09878))
